name: Revision-gated editable SelectionArea hit map

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: headed WASM/WebGPU TextArea and SelectionArea fixtures at DPR 1 and DPR 2
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Revision-gated editable SelectionArea hit map

Rebuild an editable adapter's row hit map only when text or layout geometry changed. Keep the retained map for unchanged SelectionArea paint frames; do not alter range lookup or hit-map geometry.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement plan

Run the focused TextArea and SelectionArea fixtures under headed WASM/WebGPU, then measure the existing many-participant SelectionArea fixture at DPR 1 and DPR 2. Retain only if p95 remains within five percent and screenshots preserve rendering.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected outcome

Unchanged editable participants retain their existing hit rows, while edited, resized, scrolled, and re-laid-out participants rebuild exactly as before.

measurements.target: headed WASM/WebGPU nested TextArea SelectionArea fixture; 35 repetitions per DPR with five warmups discarded

reportMarkdown:
## Revision-gated editable SelectionArea hit map

Accepted. The editable adapter now rebuilds row hits only after text or geometry changes, retaining the exact prior map on unchanged in-area paint frames. A dedicated 2,000-line TextArea-in-SelectionArea fixture passed 70/70 headed WASM/WebGPU runs and its screenshot retained the expected scrolled content.

Against the same checkpoint fixture, DPR 1 p50/p95 improved from 126.57/137.49 ms to 91.81/127.03 ms; DPR 2 improved from 134.01/135.71 ms to 79.51/89.48 ms.
